label: prf:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse
title: Proof of t beta markov frobenius collapse
html:
Proof. Proof of t beta markov frobenius collapse

Proof — completing the square

Let X \in H satisfy the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S. Write the decomposition X = (X - S \cdot 1) + S \cdot 1 and expand the Frobenius norm-squared:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X)
              = \mathrm{tr}_M\big((X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)\big)
                + 2 S \, \mathrm{tr}_M(X) - S^2 \, \mathrm{tr}_M(1).

(The scalar S \cdot 1 is central in H, so the square expands as (X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1) = X \cdot X - 2 S \cdot X + S^2 \cdot 1 even though H is non-commutative; applying the linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M term by term and rearranging gives the identity above.)

Substituting the Markov normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + 2 S^2 - S^2
             = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + S^2.

The Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is positive-semi-definite on squares (a standard property of the unique normalised trace on the symmetric semisimple Iwahori–Hecke algebra at generic q), so \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau \ge 0. Therefore

\| X \|^2_\tau \;\ge\; S^2,

with equality iff \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau = 0. By the non-degeneracy of \mathrm{tr}_M (Wenzl 1988, Jones 1987), the only Y \in H with \mathrm{tr}_M(Y \cdot Y) = 0 is Y = 0; hence X - S \cdot 1 = 0, i.e. X = S \cdot 1.

Therefore the minimum-Frobenius-norm primal-feasible element is T_\beta = S \cdot 1, with \| T_\beta \|^2_\tau = S^2. \quad\blacksquare
